# the contributor audit: regular one-full-row tetrahedral support payment

Source: `candidate d94004c6b3f150dd`, all sections. Verdict: PASS for its explicit regular, differentiable, unique proper minimizing-cut stratum. Multiple full rows and nonregular cuts remain outside scope.

The first-order multiplier equations are correctly inherited from the already independently audited source. Two distinct zero holes bound every normalized multiplier by 1/3. Euler homogeneity gives objective one. With two surviving one-zero rows, every column has positive mass outside the full row, so all its entries are strictly below one and the diagonal section map is invertible. Its restriction to the section has constant Jacobian and therefore preserves uniform centroids under the stated linear transformation.

The missing-hole centroid coordinates equal 1/3. The opposite-facet volume identity rules out a single strictly captured vertex even if other vertices lie on the cutting plane. If either missing-hole vertex is on the plane, the remaining proper incidence must form a triangle with a strictly captured missing-hole vertex of section coordinate strictly less than 1/3, a contradiction. The same triangle argument excludes a weakly captured third vertex. Thus the strict quadrilateral classification is complete. Its two exact centroid equations force the captured diagonal variables to coincide, and hence the two full-row low entries and two original centroid coordinates coincide. No assumed symmetry enters.

The marginal density 6(1-z-w) integrates to the stated cap fraction. On the section its coarea weight is the linear remaining-low-coordinate length l. The means of the two high coordinates and the conditional low-coordinate midpoint give all formulas in (5). The products and differences in (6) check directly. The inequalities C,D<=1/3 imply S>=2/3 with the correct directions, while A<1/3 gives the strict upper endpoint needed for the Bernstein parameter.

The three-coordinate support identity has an independently audited proof. After dropping the weight on the identically zero row, the transformed weights are exactly (sqrt F,sqrt(27A^2 D),sqrt(27A^2 C)). The eta construction is both a dual bound and an explicit attaining zero-diagonal matrix; its column sums and weighted row contributions are correct. Both triangle inequalities on eta are checked: the first uses the stronger specified-cap product bound, and the second uses the monotonic function 2+1/S-1/S^2 on the entire actual interval S<4/3. Squaring is legitimate because both sides are nonnegative. The resulting polynomial has the stated strictly positive lower bound.

The support value H in (11) is positive. the contributor independently expanded both the branch squared-difference identity and the full Bernstein identity (12); they vanish exactly. All five Bernstein coefficients are nonnegative for 0<rho<=1/4, with B_0>0 and 1-z>0, so the squared support difference is strictly positive. Thus H>1. The support matrices and fourth-column equality allocation construct an actual finite competitor, whose zero-diagonal row capacities equal their geometric means. This proves the strict improvement rather than merely an unattained support supremum.

Combining this stratum with the previously audited two-row case and the one-full-plus-three-zero-row payment accounts for every merged one-full-row maximum satisfying the source's regularity assumptions in d=3. No passage from these cases to arbitrary stochastic matrices or mixed-integer bodies is justified by this audit.
